Measure 1: a completion with commits, a discard, a stop and a supersession of the same run shape render four distinct departure words through the ticker's own formatter, and a promotion recording no commits does not render as promoted. Measure 2: a run promoted from a live pointer holding a folded stream emits a promoted transition whose wall seconds, token total and generation rate equal the pointer's figures read just before promotion. Measure 3: a run whose spend could not be resolved renders unlike a run that generated nothing, asserted in both directions. Any of these already met at base is recorded as met with its commit and pinned by the same test file. Every test file asserting a departure word passes at head, with base and head arms over that population recorded.
node_definition.goal: Read section 19 of crew-observability-truth first, including its comments. Much of it has landed, so measure before building. Departures already render as promoted, discarded, withdrawn or stopped, with promoted gated on a ledger row (88bd5e41a, acb45d2cb). The disposition verb reaches the committed ledger row (run r-20261003T092905759281-disposition-reaches-the-ledger-row). The ledger row carries spend resolved before the pointer is unlinked (3424f05b4). At the current main, judge each of the section's three measures on the watch-transition surface that the ticker renders: four dispositions rendered four ways, with promoted appearing only where commits are recorded; spend on the promoted transition equal to the figures on the pointer just before promotion; and an unresolvable figure rendered unlike a genuine zero. Only the unmet measures are implemented. Spend on the transition is re-derived in reckon/crew/recovery.py after promotion has emptied the pointer list, so read it from the committed ledger row or capture it before the unlink; do not derive it twice. Record per measure what was already met with its commit, and what this node changed. Write docs/evidence/fragments/crew-observability-truth/the-departure-row-says-how-and-what-it-spent.html.
